entries.title: A task you close no longer holds room on the computer it was starting on
entries.body: When you dropped or closed a task while its working copy was still being made on another computer, that computer kept counting the task's processor and memory, even after a restart. New tasks set to run on any computer could then wait for room that was never used. Closing a task now frees its room right away.
entries.noPicture: Nothing new appears: a waiting task now starts instead of waiting for room a closed task held.
